reconstructed_theorem_text: For every finite type J with decidable equality and every x in EuclideanSpace R J, put p_j(x)=e_j-x_j*x, where e_j is 1 in coordinate j and 0 elsewhere. Then sum_{j in J} ||p_j(x)||^2 = real(card J)-2*||x||^2+||x||^4. This holds for arbitrary x, without a unit-norm assumption, and includes the empty finite coordinate type.
objects: Finite type J, Euclidean vector x, standard coordinate vectors e_j, p_j(x).
domains: x in EuclideanSpace R J; finite sum over all j in J; real-valued norms.
quantifiers: For every finite J with decidable equality and every x, the identity holds.
assumptions: Only finite-type and decidable-equality instances; no norm restriction.
conclusion: Sum of squared norms of e_j-x_j*x equals card J-2||x||^2+||x||^4.
scopes: Pointwise deterministic identity for every x.
constant_dependencies: Universal numerical coefficients and cardinality; no hidden or existential constants.
context_ambiguities: None identified from the supplied statement and definition context.
